result.summary:
Completed the sensitive-action guard for the three explicit action families in English and Russian, and proved it with tests.

Product change in `forgel_code/interactive.py`: added a verb+object recognizer (`SENSITIVE_EN_RU_ACTIONS`, `CREATE_VERB_*`, `CHANGE_VERB_*`, `KEY_NOUNS`, `CONFIGURATION_NOUNS`, `SCAFFOLD_NOUNS` and their Russian stems) that `resolve()` consults after the existing marker and French/Spanish checks. It refuses a sentence that names both an action verb and the object it acts on: setting/changing a key (bare `key`/`ключ`, no credential term needed), changing configuration (bare `config`/`настройки`/`параметры`), and creating or scaffolding a project (including bare scaffolding words such as `scaffold`, `bootstrap`, `init`, `каркас`). A sentence naming only the noun stays ordinary conversation, so ordinary conversation is unaffected. The English and Russian `sensitive` refusal messages were updated so each names the action family and the explicit operation to use (`forgel-code`), in the session's language; the French and Spanish wording was left as it was and every previously guarded phrase still resolves to `sensitive`.

Tests: new `tests/test_sensitive_actions.py` drives a stand-in engine that logs every argv. Subtests assert, for every listed English and Russian form in each of the three categories, that the request is decided as `sensitive`, that the session shows the refusal without any action result (no `say` request at all, no collision with the engine's answer, one explicit-operation mention per refused phrase), that the refusal text matches the session language (`en` and `ru`), and that ordinary English and Russian messages still reach the engine and are answered. It also re-asserts the previously guarded phrases.

Verification: `python -m pytest tests -q` -> 390 passed, 643 subtests passed (existing 382 tests unchanged and passing). `CHANGELOG.md` gained one `Unreleased / Fixed` entry describing the behavior.

assumptions: The guard keys on an action verb plus the guarded object rather than on a lone noun, because the specification's Risks section forbids refusing a sentence that merely mentions a key, configuration or project; the Russian object is therefore matched by stem (inflected forms) and the English object by listed word.

The existing single refusal message key `sensitive` was extended instead of adding per-category messages, because the Non-Goals rule out redesigning refusal wording and the message already carries the structure (statement + explicit command) the acceptance criteria ask for; one message names all guarded families and the explicit operation.
The refusal names the client's own explicit command surface `forgel-code`, which is the operation surface the client exposes for these actions, so the user can act without guessing.
The `CHANGELOG.md` entry is the release-notes part this change requires; no other documentation was touched.

review.summary: The attributed change closes the audit gap in the free-text sensitive-action guard and is internally consistent. `forgel_code/interactive.py` gains a second, clearly separated family of English/Russian verb+object patterns (`SENSITIVE_EN_RU_ACTIONS`) checked by `_asks_for_explicit_action` from `resolve`, so bare key wording (`key`/`ключ` without a credential term), bare configuration wording (`config`, `preferences`, `settings`, `конфиг`/`настройк`/`параметры`), and scaffolding wording (`scaffold`, `bootstrap`, `init`, `generate`, `заскаффолди`, `каркас`) are now refused, while the pre-existing marker and four-language guards are untouched, so no earlier refusal is lost or narrowed; a sentence that names only the object without an action verb still falls through to the engine, which is what the ordinary-conversation tests exercise. The English and Russian refusal wording is extended to state that the action needs the explicit operation and to name the client's own `forgel-code` command together with the actions it performs, following the same per-language `MESSAGES` mechanism already used for the interface language, and the French/Spanish wording is left as it was. `tests/test_sensitive_actions.py` drives every listed form of the three categories in both languages through the session over a logging stand-in engine, asserts the refusal, that the refusal names `forgel-code`, and that no request reaches the engine, and also pins ordinary conversational lines that must still pass through; no test is deleted or weakened and the full suite passes per QA. `CHANGELOG.md` carries one behaviour-level release note for the change. The verb+object co-occurrence style is the design already accepted for the four-language guard in the same module, so it is not a requirement violation here.

requirements.requirement: A free-text request that asks to create, set or change key material is refused, including the bare key wording, in English and Russian.
requirements.note: KEY_NOUNS/KEY_NOUN_STEMS are paired with the changing (incl. creating) verbs; 'create a key', 'set the key', 'put a new key here', 'создай ключ', 'задай ключ', 'смени ключ' are all covered, with credential-term forms still caught by the pre-existing markers.

requirements.requirement: A free-text request that asks to change configuration is refused, including the bare configuration wording, in English and Russian.
requirements.note: CONFIGURATION_NOUNS/STEMS cover config, configuration, preferences, settings and конфиг/настройк/опци/предпочтени/параметр against the change verbs; the listed English and Russian forms resolve to the sensitive kind.

requirements.requirement: A free-text request that asks to create or scaffold a project is refused, including the bare scaffolding wording, in English and Russian.
requirements.note: SCAFFOLD_NOUNS/STEMS (project, проект, каркас, скелет, шаблон, заготовк, болванк) are paired with the creating verbs only, so scaffolding wording such as 'scaffold a project', 'init a project', 'заскаффолди проект', 'сгенерируй каркас' is refused.
